summary: Former fire tower site on Rich Mountain in Kumbrabow State Forest, Randolph County, WV; the Division of Forestry built an observation deck there in 2013. Build date unknown.

facts.status_note: Tower no longer stands; the site now has a 2013 observation deck and picnic shelter.

access.note: On Rich Mountain in the state forest. The 2013 report describes a walk in from trails, with no permanent road access yet.

visit.trail_note: 2013 report: about a two-hour hike via the Potato Hole, Meat Box and Rich Mountain Fire trails. Gates were to open to dedication guests on one Saturday, 10 a.m. to noon.

events.note: Division of Forestry built an observation deck at the former tower site, plus a small picnic shelter; about 16 acres were timbered to open the view.
Registered January 26, 2017, nominated by Brian M. Powell.

notes_for_editor: The link between the register's tower site and Rich Mountain is an inference: the register's 2013 deck note and the MetroNews report describe the same deck at the former tower site, and the MetroNews report places that site on Rich Mountain. No build date, staffing or fire history found in the pages read; the story leaves those out. Do not confuse with the Buck Knob observation platform, which elkinsrandolphwv.com mentions separately in the same forest. Access and visit details are from a 2013 report and may be out of date. Records checked: firetower.org page (read twice), county table, MetroNews 2013, wvforestry.com, Wikipedia, wvencyclopedia, CCC camp page, wvstateparks search result only.
